Maths practice that connects to school learning.

KickMaths is built for primary pupils, with a year-by-year map based on England’s National Curriculum. Children practise specific skills, from counting and number bonds to fractions, long division and Year 6 ratio. It gives families and teachers a clear way to choose relevant extra work.

Year 1

Counting and place value to 100

Addition, subtraction and number bonds to 20. Equal groups, halves, quarters, time, money, measures and shapes.

View Year 1 mathsYear 2

Two-digit place value and calculation

The 2, 5 and 10 times tables and related division. Fractions, money, five-minute time, measures and simple charts.

View Year 2 mathsYear 3

The 3, 4 and 8 times tables and related division

Three-digit numbers, column addition and subtraction. Tenths, fractions, time, perimeter and data.

View Year 3 mathsYear 4

All times tables up to 12 × 12

Four-digit column methods, fractions and decimals. Area, angles, symmetry, coordinates and graphs.

View Year 4 mathsYear 5

Long multiplication and short division

Large numbers, fractions, decimals and percentages. Measurement, angles, transformations and line graphs.

View Year 5 mathsYear 6

Long division and multi-step calculations

Fractions, percentages, ratio and introductory algebra. Four-quadrant coordinates, area, volume, pie charts and mean.

View Year 6 maths

How KickMaths supports a child who needs more practice.

Check the starting point

A short warm-up samples the chosen year. Coach checks smaller supporting skills when the answers show a gap.

Practise with clear working

Answer maths questions to take a shot. Use Coach’s written steps when an idea needs explaining. Helped answers do not earn XP.

Return to the skills that need work

Correct independent answers, mistakes and later recall build an individual learning record. Parents and teachers can inspect it in the game.

Written methods, explained

See how to work it out.

Coach shows written steps for tricky questions. Children can practise column addition and subtraction, multiplication, division and fractions, then return to a smaller supporting skill when they need it.

Explore column addition practice

Example: 8 + 5

Split 5 into 2 and 3 to make ten first.

  1. 8 + 2 = 10
  2. 10 + 3 = 13

Small steps make the method visible.

Designed to make extra practice easier to access.

Dyslexia-friendly mode

A clearly labelled setting changes the font and spacing, softens the reading background and reduces visual distractions.

Reports for parents and teachers

See examples of practised questions, independent answers, questions needing help and each skill’s secure checklist.

Frequently asked questions

What is KickMaths?

KickMaths is an online football maths game for primary pupils in Years 1–6. Children answer maths questions, score goals, earn cosmetic rewards and build a learning record that parents and teachers can review.

Is KickMaths based on the UK primary curriculum?

KickMaths is designed for UK primary pupils. Its Year 1–6 map follows England’s National Curriculum for mathematics. Families and teachers elsewhere in the UK can choose the topics and practice level that match their school’s teaching.

Is KickMaths free to play?

Yes. KickMaths is free to play during beta for families and schools. A paid version is coming soon; pricing and launch details will be announced later.

Can KickMaths help when a child has gaps in maths?

Coach uses the child’s answers to identify skills needing more practice and can check earlier supporting skills. Worked steps and focused practice give the child another way to approach an unfamiliar method.
